cards.explanation: The answer is a warning from God. God tells Ezekiel, the prophet, “Whenever you hear a word from My mouth, give them a warning from Me.” That's the whole watchman job, friends. Ezekiel doesn't make up the message. He passes along what he hears.

The answer is False. The wicked man doesn't get a pass. The text says “…that wicked man will die in his iniquity…” On top of that, God says, “…I will hold you responsible for his blood.” Staying quiet isn't a safe option for the watchman, friends.

The answer is Ezekiel. God says, “…I will hold you responsible for his blood.” The “you” is Ezekiel, the one who was supposed to warn the man and didn't. That's what makes the watchman's job so serious, friends. It's a heavy line.

The answer is that he has saved himself. God says, “But if you warn a wicked man and he does not turn from his wickedness and his wicked way, he will die in his iniquity, but you will have saved yourself.” Ezekiel did the job he was given, friends. The man's choice is the man's own.

The answer is False. God says that if Ezekiel didn't warn him, “…he will die in his sin, and the righteous acts he did will not be remembered.” Then God adds, “…I will hold you responsible for his blood.” That's a serious line, friends, so I'll just let it sit.

The answer is that he will indeed live. God says, “…he will indeed live because he heeded your warning, and you will have saved yourself.” The warning worked because the man listened, friends. After the heavy warnings in this passage, this one feels like a deep breath.

The answer is True. Ezekiel says, “…the glory of the LORD was present there, like the glory I had seen by the River Kebar, and I fell facedown.” He had seen glory like that before, friends. Even so, it puts him on the ground.

The answer is into his house to shut himself in. The Spirit sets Ezekiel on his feet and says, “Go, shut yourself inside your house.” It's a strange order for a watchman, friends. I think he wasn't expecting that one, and I bet I wouldn't have been either.

The answer is rebuking the people. God says, “I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth, and you will be silent and unable to rebuke them, though they are a rebellious house.” The silence is about rebuking them, friends. And God isn't finished, because He says He will open Ezekiel's mouth when He speaks with him.

The answer is True. God says, “Whoever listens, let him listen; and whoever refuses, let him refuse, for they are a rebellious house.” Ezekiel is told to say, “This is what the Lord GOD says.” The warning gets given either way, friends. This is the end of the story of Ezekiel's call, but there's more of his book ahead.
